arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ العُودَ، ثُمَّ قَطَفَ حَفْنَةً مِنَ العُشْبِ.
english: The squirrel climbed the wooden stick, then picked a handful of grass.
reason: Plausible in an animal story, with the squirrel gathering grass; the translation matches.

arabic: شَافَ الوَلَدُ فَرَاشَةً عَلَى سَبَّابَتِهِ، فَدَهِشَ وَصَمَتَ بُرْهَةً.
english: The boy saw a butterfly on his index finger, so he was astonished and fell silent for a moment.
reason: A coherent scene. شاف is colloquial but natural, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: هَاتِ يَا بَابَا الشَّوْكَةَ وَالخَرْدَلَ وَالزُّبْدَةَ، فَالبَاذِنْجَانُ جَاهِزٌ الآنَ.
english: Dad, bring the fork, the mustard and the butter, the eggplant is ready now.
reason: A plausible request while serving food; the translation matches.

arabic: يَمْنَحُ الطِّبُّ الحَدِيثُ المُوَاطِنَ رِعَايَةً وَشِفَاءً مِنَ المَرَضِ.
english: Modern medicine gives the citizen care and recovery from disease.
reason: Grammatical and plausible formal Arabic, accurately translated.

arabic: شِرَاءُ التَّنُّورَةِ مُتْعِبٌ، فَالمَقَاسُ خَاطِئٌ وَالحَجْمُ صَغِيرٌ جِدًّا.
english: Buying the skirt is tiring, since the size is wrong and the fit is too small.
reason: The sizing complaint is coherent despite some redundancy. The translation preserves its meaning.

arabic: أَفَلَ الهِلَالُ، فَخَلَا المَشْهَدُ مِنَ الضِّيَاءِ وَغَيَّمَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ.
english: The crescent set, so the scene was left empty of light and everything clouded over.
reason: Acceptable literary imagery describing darkness and clouding; the translation preserves that imagery.

arabic: لَدَى الرَّجُلِ عِمَارَةٌ عَلَى مَسَافَةٍ مِنَ الجِسْرِ، وَثَمَنُهَا نِصْفُ مِلْيُونِ دُولَارٍ.
english: The man has a building some distance from the bridge, and its price is half a million dollars.
reason: Natural description of property location and price, accurately translated.

arabic: نَظَّمَتِ الفِرْقَةُ مُؤْتَمَرًا، وَشَمِلَ تَوْفِيرُ الاِسْتِضَافَةِ كُلَّ الأَعْضَاءِ.
english: The group organized a conference, and providing hosting included all the members.
reason: Somewhat bureaucratic phrasing, but coherently states that hosting covered every member. The translation matches.

arabic: بَاحَ الشَّيْخُ بِمُعَانَاتِهِ فِي سِجْنٍ قَاسٍ شَاخَ فِيهِ.
english: The old man revealed his suffering in a harsh prison in which he grew old.
reason: Grammatical and plausible description of suffering and aging in prison; accurately translated.

arabic: يَا تُرَى مَا حِيلَةُ الثَّعْلَبِ الأَجْرَبِ الَّذِي نَحُلَ وَسَخِرَ مِنْهُ كُلُّ وَحْشٍ؟
english: I wonder, what is the trick of the mangy fox who grew thin and was mocked by every beast?
reason: Plausible in a fable. حيلة can mean a trick or stratagem, as translated.

arabic: رَاجَ التَّزَلُّجُ فِي الهِنْدِ وَلَا سِيَّمَا وَسَطَ الطُّلَّابِ، فَلَدَيْهِمْ مَيْلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
english: Skiing has spread in India, especially among students, since they have an inclination toward it.
reason: A plausible statement about a sport's popularity. Skiing is a valid contextual reading of التزلج.

arabic: قَرَصَ الوَلَدُ لِحْيَةَ جَدِّهِ عَبَثًا، فَصَاحَ الجَدُّ وَبَسَرَ.
english: The boy pinched his grandfather's beard in mischief, so the grandfather shouted and scowled.
reason: A coherent scene. بَسَرَ correctly means scowled, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: قَدِمَ الْمُصَوِّرُ إِلَى مَقَرِّ الرِّئَاسَةِ وَمَعَهُ مَجْمُوعَةٌ مِنَ الأَصْحَابِ.
english: The photographer arrived at the presidency headquarters, and with him was a group of friends.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the English accurately conveys the meaning.

arabic: تَجَاهَلَ الْمُشْرِفُ اعْتِرَاضَ الطَّالِبِ عَلَى تَحْدِيدِ مَكَانِ الاِمْتِحَانِ، وَلَمْ يَرْضَ الطَّالِبُ.
english: The supervisor ignored the student's objection to fixing the location of the exam, and the student was not satisfied.
reason: A coherent sentence with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: كَانَ ظُهُورُ الشِّهَابِ الْمُتَّقِدِ فِي الظَّلَامِ مُعْجِزَةً مُمْتِعَةً جِدًّا.
english: The appearance of the glowing meteor in the darkness was a very enjoyable miracle.
reason: The description is expressive but plausible, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: أَخَذَ الْحَلَّاقُ الْمِقَصَّ وَالْمُشْطَ وَخَطَّ حَاجِبَ الصَّبِيِّ.
english: The barber took the scissors and the comb and shaped the boy's eyebrow.
reason: خَطَّ حَاجِبَ means drawing or marking the eyebrow, not clearly shaping it. هذّب حاجب الصبي would express the intended grooming action naturally.

arabic: طَالَمَا حَافَظَ النَّادِلُ عَلَى جِدِّهِ فَلَنْ يَقَعَ فِي الْفَشَلِ.
english: As long as the waiter keeps his diligence, he will not fall into failure.

arabic: لِلصَّبِيِّ ذِكْرَى مُؤَثِّرَةٌ عَنْ خِلَّةٍ مُخَلِّصَةٍ دَامَتْ مَعَ جَارِهِ.
english: The boy has a moving memory of a sincere friendship that lasted with his neighbor.
reason: Friendship is خُلَّة, not خِلَّة, and sincere is مُخْلِصَة, not مُخَلِّصَة. The English translates the apparent intention rather than the Arabic as written.

arabic: حَجَزَ الْمِعْمَارُ مَكَانًا وَأَخَذَ التَّأْشِيرَةَ ثُمَّ اتَّجَهَ إِلَى نِرْوَيجَ.
english: The architect booked a place and got the visa, then headed to Norway.
reason: The travel sequence is plausible and accurately translated; النرويج is the more usual country name.

arabic: فِي الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ، نُطْقُ الْبَا يَتِمُّ بِالشَّفَةِ فَقَطْ وَلَيْسَ بِاللِّسَانِ.
english: In phonetics, the pronunciation of Ba is done with the lip only, not with the tongue.
reason: The letter name is misspelled: standard Arabic requires الْبَاءِ rather than الْبَا here. The English conveys the intended statement.

arabic: عَاقَبَ الْوَزِيرُ الرَّجُلَ الَّذِي خَلَطَ الْقَمْحَ بِمَادَّةٍ مَغْشُوشَةٍ.
english: The minister punished the man who mixed the wheat with an adulterated substance.
reason: A plausible statement about food adulteration, accurately translated.

arabic: قَفَزَ الصَّبِيُّ إِلَى الشَّبَكَةِ ثُمَّ أَلْقَى الْمِضْرَبَ وَسَعَلَ.
english: The boy jumped to the net, then threw down the racket and coughed.
reason: The actions form a plausible sports scene, and the translation matches.

arabic: شَبَّ الصَّبِيُّ وَتَطَوَّرَتْ عَضَلَتُهُ لِأَنَّهُ رَكَضَ عِشْرِينَ مِتْرًا كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
english: The boy grew up and his muscle developed because he ran twenty metres every morning.
reason: The exercise distance is unusually short and the singular muscle is somewhat awkward, but the statement remains possible and is accurately translated.

arabic: دَعَمَ الْوَزِيرُ إِيقَافَ حَبْسِ الْفَقِيرِ الْبَائِسِ لِأَنَّ حَالَتَهُ مُؤْلِمَةٌ.
english: The minister supported stopping the imprisonment of the miserable poor man because his case is painful.
reason: The wording is somewhat formal but coherent, grammatical, and accurately translated.

arabic: خَصَمَ الخَيَّاطُ هَذَا الصَّبَاحَ سَبْعِينَ دُولَاراً مِنَ البِذْلَةِ وَالحِذَاءِ.
english: This morning the tailor deducted seventy dollars from the suit and the shoes.
reason: Plausible discount on clothing; omitting an explicit reference to the price is understandable.

arabic: كَانَ الجَارُ جَوْعَانَ بَعْدَ الصِّيَامِ، فَأَطْعَمَ الصَّائِمَاتِ أَوَّلاً.
english: The neighbor was hungry after the fast, but he fed the fasting women first.
reason: Grammatical and coherent. English 'but' reasonably conveys the implied contrast.

arabic: اخْتَبَرَ المُتَخَصِّصُ مُحْتَوَى الخَلِيطِ فِي التَّجْرِبَةِ، ثُمَّ سَجَّلَ مُعَدَّلَ الِارْتِفَاعِ.
english: The specialist tested the content of the mixture in the experiment, then recorded the rate of rise.
reason: A plausible experimental procedure, accurately translated.

arabic: حَرَثَ الجَارُ البَرَّ، ثُمَّ سَنَا الزَّانَ، وَكَانَ العِجْلُ هَادِئاً.
english: The neighbor plowed the land, then watered the beech tree, and the calf was calm.
reason: A coherent agricultural scene. سنا is rare but has an attested watering sense: [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/محرك-البحث/معجم/dic-337/معنى%20سنا).

arabic: المَطْحَنَةُ القَدِيمَةُ ثَرْوَةُ الجَارِ، وَمَا زَالَتْ تَطْحَنُ مَدَّ قَرْنٍ.
english: The old mill is the neighbor's wealth, and it has kept on grinding for a century.
reason: مَدَّ قَرْنٍ does not correctly express 'for a century'; use مُدَّةَ قَرْنٍ.

arabic: تَوَفَّى الجَارُ، فَقَبَرُوهُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ هَادِئٍ، وَأَمَلْنَا لَهُ الفِرْدَوْسَ.
english: The neighbor died, so they buried him in a quiet place, and we hoped paradise for him.
reason: تَوَفَّى is active and does not mean 'died' here. The required form is تُوُفِّيَ الجَارُ.

arabic: شَرُفَ الأَمِيرُ لِأَنَّهُ حَكَمَ بِنَزَاهَةٍ وَمَنَعَ القَمْعَ فِي كُلِّ مَجَالٍ.
english: The prince became noble because he ruled with integrity and prevented repression in every field.
reason: A plausible statement about a ruler acquiring honor through just government.

arabic: لَمْ يَرْغَبِ البَطَلُ فِي الصِّرَاعِ فَسَالَمَ الشِّرِّيرَ، لَكِنَّ الشِّرِّيرَ خَادَعَهُ.
english: The hero did not desire conflict, so he made peace with the villain, but the villain deceived him.
reason: Grammatical, coherent storytelling with an accurate translation.

arabic: أَيْقَظَ البَابَا الأَمِيرَةَ بِقُبْلَةٍ وَهَمَسَ لَهَا، فَكَانَ مِزَاجُهَا جَيِّداً.
english: Dad woke the princess with a kiss and whispered to her, so her mood was good.
reason: Plausible in a family or story context, taking البابا in its informal sense of 'Dad'.

arabic: اسْتَعْمَلَ الجَارُ لَزْقَةً عَلَى حَنْجَرَتِهِ، فَأَخْفَضَ الخَدَرُ حَاسَّةَ الأَلَمِ.
english: The neighbor used a plaster on his throat, and the numbness lowered the sense of pain.
reason: Understandable as a numbing medicinal plaster applied over the throat; the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: رَمَّ النَّجَّارُ فِي الجَرَاجِ مُؤَخَّرَةَ العَرَبَةِ وَعَجَلَتَهَا بِقَضِيبٍ خَاصٍّ.
english: In the garage, the carpenter repaired the rear of the cart and its wheel with a special rod.
reason: Plausible repair of a wooden cart. رَمَّ means 'repaired': [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/محرك-البحث/معجم/dic-19/رم).

arabic: تَصَوَّرَ الطَّالِبُ العَجَمِيُّ أَنَّ الأَبْجَدِيَّةَ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ مُعَقَّدَةٌ جِدّاً فَتَذَمَّرَ.
english: The foreign student imagined that the English alphabet was very complex, so he complained.
reason: A plausible learner's reaction. 'Foreign' reasonably renders العجمي here, though 'non-Arab' is more precise.

arabic: الطَّاوُوقُ مَعَ بَهَارٍ وَنَعْنَاعٍ هُوَ أَكْلِي المُفَضَّلُ، وَهَذَا ذَوْقِي.
english: Tawook with spices and mint is my favorite food, and that is my taste.
reason: A plausible statement of food preference; the translation matches.

arabic: جَهَّزَتِ الجَدَّةُ المَنْسَفَ وَالمُقَبِّلَاتِ لِلْعَشَاءِ، وَحَرَّكَتِ البامْيا فِي زَبْدِيَّةٍ.
english: The grandmother prepared the mansaf and the appetizers for dinner, and stirred the okra in a bowl.
reason: Grammatical and coherent descriptions of preparing and stirring food.

arabic: كَنَسَتِ الفَتَاةُ فَضْلَةَ الهَمْسْتَرِ وَالجُرَذِ بِالمِكْنَسَةِ، ثُمَّ مَسَحَتِ الأَرْضَ.
english: The girl swept up the droppings of the hamster and the rat with the broom, then wiped the floor.
reason: A plausible cleaning scene. فضلة can refer to animal waste.

arabic: وَجَدَ الرَّجُلُ تَجْعِيدَةً فَظِيعَةً فِي الجَلَّابِيَّةِ وَفِي الجِينْزِ، فَدَمْدَمَ.
english: The man found a terrible wrinkle in the robe and in the jeans, so he grumbled.
reason: Wrinkles in clothing prompting grumbling is plausible, and the translation preserves the meaning.

arabic: تَوَقَّعَ الرَّجُلُ عَوْدَتَهُ المُقْبِلَةَ بَعْدَ زَمَانٍ، فَاسْتَرْخَى عَلَى مَهَلٍ.
english: The man anticipated his upcoming return after a long time, so he relaxed at leisure.
reason: Slightly cumbersome wording, but a plausible statement about anticipating a later return and relaxing.

arabic: بَدَأَ انْتِحَابُ الفَتَاةِ العَاطِفِيَّةِ لِأَنَّهَا زَعْلَانَةٌ، ثُمَّ ابْتَسَمَتْ مَبْسُوطَةً.
english: The emotional girl began sobbing because she was upset, then smiled, happy.

arabic: سَجَدَتِ الرَّعِيَّةُ لِلْإِلٰهِ فِي الأُسْطُورَةِ، ثُمَّ دَافَعَتْ عَنْ بَلَدِهَا مِنَ العَدُوِّ.
english: In the legend, the subjects bowed down to the god, then defended their country from the enemy.
reason: A coherent legendary scene. Feminine singular agreement with الرعية is correct.

arabic: أَحَبَّ القَانِصُ التَّشْوِيقَ، فَوَجَدَ فِي سُطُورِ القِصَّةِ لُغْزًا عَنْ خَبِيئَةٍ.
english: The hunter loved suspense, so he found in the lines of the story a riddle about a hidden secret.
reason: A hunter enjoying a suspenseful story is plausible. خبيئة can denote something concealed or secret.

arabic: غَمَرَ الثَّلْجُ المُتَجَمِّدُ الأَرْضَ، فَنَضَبَتِ المُؤْنَةُ وَكَانَتِ الخَيْمَةُ خَاوِيَةً.
english: The frozen snow flooded the ground, so the supplies ran dry and the tent was empty.
reason: A plausible scene of snow cover and depleted provisions. 'Flooded' conveys غمر figuratively, though 'blanketed' would be more idiomatic.

arabic: اِعْتَمَلَ الطَّحَّانُونَ النَّشِيطُونَ بِمَشَقَّةٍ، وَوَاظَبَ اثْنَانِ مِنْهُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ.
english: The active millers worked with great hardship, and two of them persevered in that.
reason: اعتمل is a valid, literary verb meaning to work. The sentence and translation are coherent.

arabic: أَمَامَ عِنَادِ الوَلَدِ وَلَامُبَالَاتِهِ كَانَ المُؤَنِّبُ الصَّبُورُ مُفْحَمًا جِدًّا.
english: Before the boy's stubbornness and indifference, the patient reproacher was completely silenced.
reason: Formal but plausible: the boy's behavior leaves the person reprimanding him speechless.

arabic: لَاحَ بَهَاءُ القِنْدِيلِ المُنْعَكِسِ عَلَى الطَّاقِ المُسْتَدِيرِ فِي الرُّكْنِ.
english: The brilliance of the lantern, reflected on the round arch, gleamed in the corner.
reason: A plausible literary description of lantern light and its reflection on an arch.

arabic: تَسَلَّقَ السِّنْجَابُ العِمَارَةَ فِي بُرْهَةٍ، فَدَهِشَ الوَلَدُ وَالرَّجُلُ أَيْضًا.
english: The squirrel climbed the building in a moment, and the boy and the man were both astonished.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately conveys the event and reactions.

arabic: قَطَفَتِ الجَدَّةُ حَفْنَةً مِنَ العُشْبِ البَلَدِيِّ، وَأَضَافَتْهَا إِلَى الحُمُّصِ.
english: Grandmother picked a handful of the local herb and added it to the hummus.
reason: A plausible cooking scene with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: قَلَعَ الجَدُّ الشَّوْكَةَ مِنْ سَبَّابَةِ الوَلَدِ، فَصَمَتَ الوَلَدُ مِنَ الخَوْفِ.
english: Grandfather pulled the thorn out of the boy's index finger, and the boy went quiet out of fear.
reason: Removing a thorn and the boy becoming quiet from fear form a coherent scene; the translation matches.

arabic: خَالَفَ العَمُّ النَّبَاتِيُّ الطِّبَّ الحَدِيثَ، وَاسْتَعَانَ بِالكَمُّونِ وَالقِرْفَةِ لِلشِّفَاءِ مِنَ المَرَضِ.
english: My vegetarian uncle went against modern medicine and turned to cumin and cinnamon to recover from the illness.
reason: The Arabic is grammatical and plausible, but العَمّ means 'the uncle'; 'my uncle' adds a possessive relationship not specified in the sentence.

arabic: عَجِبَ الوَلَدُ مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الهِلَالِ، ثُمَّ أَفَلَ الهِلَالُ فَشَعَرَ بِالحُزْنِ.
english: The boy marveled at the crescent's glow, then the crescent set and he felt sad.
reason: A natural narrative description; the translation accurately preserves the sequence and emotion.

arabic: يَا تُرَى، هَلْ تَشْمَلُ رِعَايَةُ الطَّبِيعَةِ حِمَايَةَ الفَرَاشَاتِ المُنْتَشِرَةِ هُنَا؟
english: I wonder, does caring for nature include protecting the butterflies found all over here?

arabic: خَلَا السِّجْنُ التَّارِيخِيُّ مِنَ الحَرَسِ، وَالآنَ يُنَظِّمُ المُوَظَّفُونَ فِيهِ زِيَارَاتٍ سِيَاحِيَّةً.
english: The historic prison has no guards anymore, and now the staff organize tourist visits there.
reason: A coherent description of a former prison used for tourism, translated accurately.

arabic: قَبْلَ شِرَاءِ الخِزَانَةِ، اِسْتَعْمَلَتِ السَّيِّدَةُ آلَةً لِقِيَاسِ حَجْمِ الرُّكْنِ.
english: Before buying the closet, the lady used a tool to measure the size of the corner.
reason: Measuring a corner before buying a closet is plausible, and the translation matches.

arabic: هَاتِ يَا اِبْنِي نِصْفَ الزُّبْدَةِ وَرُبْعَ وِعَاءِ الخَرْدَلِ مِنَ الخِزَانَةِ.
english: Son, bring me half the butter and a quarter of the mustard jar from the cupboard.
reason: A plausible household request; the quarter-jar quantity is understood as referring to its contents in both languages.

arabic: رَئِيسُ الهِنْدِ مَنَحَ مِلْيُونَ دُولَارٍ لِتَوْفِيرِ الدَّوَاءِ وَالمُؤْنَةِ لِلمُوَاطِنِينَ.
english: India's president gave a million dollars to provide medicine and supplies for citizens.
reason: Grammatical and plausible as a report of funding; the translation matches the Arabic.

arabic: حَفَلَتِ القَاعَةُ بِالأَعْضَاءِ الأَجَانِبِ أَثْنَاءَ اسْتِضَافَةِ المُؤْتَمَرِ، وَلَا سِيَّمَا مِنَ اليَمَنِ.
english: The hall was crowded with foreign members while it hosted the conference, especially members from Yemen.
reason: The reference to members from Yemen uses understandable ellipsis; the translation accurately makes it explicit.

arabic: شَاخَ الجَدُّ وَنَحُلَ مِنَ المُعَانَاةِ مَعَ المَرَضِ، لَكِنَّ الدَّوَاءَ شَفَاهُ تَدْرِيجِيًّا.
english: Grandfather aged and grew thin from suffering with the illness, but the medicine gradually healed him.
reason: Grammatical and coherent, with an accurate translation of the illness and gradual recovery.

arabic: قَدِمَ المِعْمَارُ إِلَى المَدِينَةِ، ثُمَّ تَمَّ الصَّرْحُ الَّذِي يَبْلُغُ عِشْرِينَ مِتْرًا.
english: The architect came to the city, then the edifice, which reaches twenty metres, was completed.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; مِعْمَار can mean architect, and تَمَّ means was completed.

arabic: خَلَطَ النَّادِلُ القَمْحَ وَالزَّيْتَ فِي ظَرْفٍ، فَأَصْبَحَ الغَدَاءُ مَالِحًا جِدًّا.
english: The waiter mixed the wheat and the oil in a container, so the lunch became very salty.
reason: Mixing wheat and oil does not explain the lunch becoming very salty; the causal connection is incoherent without substantial missing context.

arabic: أَدْرُسُ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ فِي النِّرْوِيجِ، لَكِنَّ تَأْشِيرَتِي مَحْدُودَةٌ وَتَنْتَهِي فِي نُوفَمْبِر.
english: I study phonetics in Norway, but my visa is limited and ends in November.
reason: A plausible statement about studying abroad and a visa's limited validity. The translation matches.

arabic: دَفَّ الطَّاوُوسُ وَأَدَارَ ذَنَبَهُ، فَشَاهَدَهُ المُصَوِّرُ المُتَلَهِّفُ فِي ذُهُولٍ.
english: The peacock flapped its wings and turned its tail, and the eager photographer watched it in astonishment.
reason: A coherent wildlife scene. دَفَّ can describe a bird moving its wings, so 'flapped its wings' is valid.

arabic: فِي العِيَادَةِ سَعَلَ الصَّبِيُّ، فَتَحَرَّى الخَبِيرُ لِسَانَهُ وَشَفَتَيْهِ بِجِدٍّ.
english: In the clinic the boy coughed, so the expert examined his tongue and lips seriously.
reason: تَحَرَّى لسانه وشفتيه is an unsuitable expression for physically examining these body parts. فَحَصَ would convey the English meaning naturally.

arabic: يَعْنِي، كَانَ ظُهُورُ الشِّهَابِ المُتَّقِدِ فِي الظَّلَامِ مُعْجِزَةً لِكُلِّ مَنْ شَاهَدَهُ.
english: I mean, the appearance of the burning meteor in the darkness was a miracle for everyone who watched it.
reason: Grammatical and plausible as an emotional description of a meteor sighting. The translation is accurate.

arabic: خَفِيَ المِقَصُّ وَالمُشْطُ فِي الدُّرْجِ، فَغَيَّظَ ذَلِكَ الحَلَّاقَ طَوَالَ الصَّبَاحِ.
english: The scissors and the comb were hidden in the drawer, and that angered the barber all morning.
reason: A plausible account of a barber frustrated by hidden tools. Agreement and translation are correct.

arabic: الجَيْشُ أَطَاحَ بِالرِّئَاسَةِ، فَانْدَلَعَ الاعْتِرَاضُ فِي المَدِينَةِ طَوَالَ أُسْبُوعٍ.
english: The army overthrew the presidency, so opposition broke out in the city for a whole week.
reason: The political scene is coherent. اندلع الاعتراض is less usual than اندلعت الاحتجاجات but remains understandable and plausible.

arabic: اِعْتَصَرَتِ الجَارَةُ التُّوتَ ثُمَّ رَخَّتْهُ، فَلَمْ يَرْضَ أَحْمَدُ بِهَذَا الكُوبِ المَغْشُوشِ.
english: The neighbour squeezed the mulberries and then watered them down, so Ahmed was not satisfied with this adulterated cup.
reason: A plausible account of diluted fruit juice; التوت and الكوب allow ordinary contextual reference to their juice and contents. [The Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/رخخ) confirms رَخَّ الشرابَ means to mix or dilute a drink.

arabic: عَاقَبَ المُشْرِفُ الطَّالِبَ البَائِسَ، لَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَطْرُدْهُ بَعْدَ فَشَلِهِ فِي الامْتِحَانِ.
english: The supervisor punished the miserable student, but he did not expel him after his failure in the exam.
reason: Grammatical, coherent, and accurately translated.

arabic: حِكَايَةُ المُسَلْسَلِ مُمْتِعَةٌ وَمُؤَثِّرَةٌ، فَشَاهَدَتْهَا مَجْمُوعَةُ الأَصْحَابِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
english: The series' story is enjoyable and moving, so the group of friends watched it every morning.
reason: A plausible viewing habit. The feminine pronoun in شاهدتها correctly refers to حكاية, rendered as 'it' in English.

arabic: عِنْدَ إِيَابِ الوَالِدِ عَانَقَتْهُ الفَتَاةُ، فَدَامَتْ هَذِهِ الذِّكْرَى مَعَهَا حَتَّى شَبَّتْ.
english: When the father returned, the girl hugged him, and this memory stayed with her until she grew up.
reason: A coherent childhood memory, with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: رَمَّ المُتَخَصِّصُ عَجَلَةَ العَرَبَةِ القَدِيمَةِ فِي الجَرَاجِ بِسَبْعِينَ دُولَارًا فَقَطْ.
english: The specialist repaired the old cart's wheel in the garage for only seventy dollars.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; رَمَّ means repaired or restored.

arabic: لَمْ يَتَذَمَّرِ المُرَاهِقُ الجَوْعَانُ مِنَ الصِّيَامِ، فَقَدْ كَانَ مُعْتَادًا عَلَيْهِ.
english: The hungry teenager did not complain about fasting, because he was used to it.
reason: Natural learner-friendly sentence with an accurate translation.

arabic: اخْتَارَ أَحْمَدُ بِذْلَةً إِنْجِلِيزِيَّةً بُنِّيَّةً، فَخَصَمَ لَهُ الخَيَّاطُ سِتَّةَ دُولَارَاتٍ.
english: Ahmed chose a brown English suit, so the tailor took six dollars off for him.

arabic: فَاضَتِ القَنَاةُ بَعْدَ الإِعْصَارِ، فَنَزَلَ الجَارُ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَأَنْقَذَ العِجْلَ الغَارِقَ.
english: The canal overflowed after the hurricane, so the neighbor quickly went down and rescued the drowning calf.
reason: Coherent rescue scenario; the English accurately conveys the Arabic.

arabic: شَاهَدْنَا فِلْمًا مُضْحِكًا جِدًّا، فَتَحَوَّلَ مِزَاجُ بَابَا المُرْهَقِ إِلَى سُرُورٍ.
english: We watched a very funny film, and Dad's tired mood turned into happiness.
reason: Plausible and grammatical. المُرْهَقِ describes Dad; the English conveys the intended change in his mood.

arabic: مَا زَالَ الخَدَرُ فِي حَلْقِي، مَعَ أَنَّ الإِجْرَاءَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُعَقَّدًا.
english: My throat is still numb, even though the procedure was not complicated.
reason: Natural description of lingering numbness after a procedure; accurately translated.

arabic: وَفْقًا لِلرَّادْيُو، حَصَلَ ارْتِفَاعٌ فِي صِنَاعَةِ البِتْرُولِ بِمُعَدَّلٍ مُتَوَسِّطٍ.
english: According to the radio, the petroleum industry saw a rise at a moderate rate.
reason: The economic wording is somewhat vague but coherent and grammatically acceptable; the translation matches.

arabic: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، أَيْقَظَتِ الأَمِيرَةُ جَوَادَهَا بِقُبْلَةٍ، وَدَاعَبَتْهُ، ثُمَّ هَمَسَتْ: أَهْلًا.
english: In the morning, the princess woke her horse with a kiss, stroked it, and then whispered: "Hello."
reason: Plausible affectionate interaction with a horse, especially in a story; accurately translated.

arabic: هَلْ تَتَصَوَّرُ عَالَمًا يَكُونُ فِيهِ النَّمِرُ مُنْدَثِرًا بَعْدَ قَرْنٍ؟
english: Can you imagine a world where the tiger is extinct a century from now?
reason: Grammatical, coherent question about future extinction; accurately translated.

arabic: النَّزَاهَةُ هِيَ المَبْدَأُ الأَوَّلُ فِي مَجَالِنَا، فَمَنْ خَادَعَ لَا يَسْتَحِقُّ مُكَافَأَةً.
english: Integrity is the first principle in our field, so whoever cheats does not deserve a reward.
reason: Natural statement about integrity and rewards; the translation is accurate.

arabic: رَغِبَ الجَارُ اللَّهِمُ فِي كُلِّ طَعَامِ المَأْدُبَةِ: الرُّزِّ المَنْدِي وَالفُلْفُلِ المَحْشِيِّ.
english: The greedy neighbor wanted all the food at the feast: the mandi rice and the stuffed peppers.
reason: لَهِم is a valid adjective meaning gluttonous or greedy. The sentence and its translation are acceptable.

arabic: حَكَمَ الأَمِيرُ المَدِينَةَ بِالقَمْعِ، فَهَاجَرَ رِجَالُهَا بِثَرْوَتِهِمْ إِلَى السُّودَانِ.
english: The emir ruled the city through repression, so its men emigrated to Sudan with their wealth.
reason: Grammatical and plausible political scenario; the English accurately reflects the Arabic.

arabic: طَلَبْتُ سَنْدَوِيتْشَ طَاوُوقٍ وَمُقَبِّلَاتٍ بِالنَّعْنَاعِ، لَكِنَّ الطَّاوُوقَ كَانَ مُتَجَمِّدًا.
english: I ordered a tawook sandwich and appetizers with mint, but the tawook was frozen.
reason: Grammatical and plausible restaurant complaint; the translation is accurate.

arabic: جَهَّزَتِ الجَدَّةُ فِي الأَضْحَى المَنْسَفَ وَالصَّيَّادِيَةَ وَالبَامْيَا بِبَهَارٍ مِنْ لُبْنَانَ.
english: For Eid al-Adha, grandmother prepared mansaf, sayadieh and okra with spices from Lebanon.
reason: A plausible holiday meal. بهار can refer collectively to spices or seasoning.

arabic: يَعْتَاشُ الهَمْسْتَرُ عَلَى الخَضْرَاوَاتِ وَالإِجَّاصِ فَقَطْ، وَزَبْدِيَّتُهُ خَاوِيَةٌ الآنَ.
english: The hamster lives only on vegetables and pears, and its bowl is empty now.
reason: A coherent description of a hamster's diet and empty bowl; accurately translated.

arabic: تَتَحَرَّكُ السُّلَحْفَاةُ المُتَثَاقِلَةُ عَلَى مَهَلٍ فِي قَنَاةِ المَزْرَعَةِ الضَّحْلَةِ، ثُمَّ تَتَوَقَّفُ.
english: The sluggish turtle moves slowly in the farm's shallow channel, then stops.
reason: Natural, grammatical description of a turtle moving through a shallow channel.

arabic: وَجَدَتِ العَجُوزُ فَضَلَاتِ جُرَذٍ فِي التُّوَالِيتِ، فَكَنَسَتِ الأَرْضَ ثُمَّ مَسَحَتْهَا.
english: The old woman found rat droppings in the toilet, so she swept the floor and then wiped it.
reason: A plausible cleaning scene; التواليت can denote the bathroom, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: تَشَاوَرَ الأَصْدِقَاءُ النَّشِيطُونَ فِي غَرَابَةِ اللُّغْزِ، لَكِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُفْحَمِينَ أَمَامَهُ.
english: The active friends discussed the riddle's strangeness, but they were left speechless before it.

arabic: لَا مَثِيلَ لِبَهَاءِ الطَّاقِ المُسْتَدِيرِ فِي هَذِهِ الكَاتِدْرَائِيَّةِ الأُورُوبِّيَّةِ.
english: Nothing equals the splendor of the round arch in this European cathedral.
reason: A grammatical, plausible expression of admiration for cathedral architecture.

arabic: فِي أُسْطُورَةٍ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ البَعِيدِ، وَجَدَ الطَّحَّانُ خَبِيئَةً تَحْتَ الأَرْضِ.
english: In a legend from long ago, the miller found a hidden treasure under the ground.
reason: A coherent story sentence; خبيئة can denote concealed valuables or treasure.

arabic: نَمَّ بَعْضُ الأَصْدِقَاءِ عَلَى العَزْبَاءِ، لَكِنَّهَا دَافَعَتْ عَنِ اسْتِغْنَائِهَا عَنِ الرَّجُلِ بِعِنَادٍ.
english: Some friends gossiped about the single woman, but she stubbornly defended her not needing a man.
reason: Somewhat formal but plausible. The English conveys the gossip and her insistence on independence.

arabic: الطَّبَّاخُ مُولَعٌ بِعَصِيرِ العِرْقْسُوسِ، فَهُوَ مُهَدِّئٌ لَهُ إِذَا كَانَ زَعْلَانَ.
english: The cook loves licorice juice, because it calms him when he is upset.
reason: Plausible and understandable, with the informal زعلان fitting the stated meaning. Accurately translated.

arabic: أَوْشَكَتِ المُؤْنَةُ أَنْ تَنْضَبَ، فَتَوَقَّعْنَا عَوْدَةَ الرَّاعِي فِي الجُمْعَةِ المُقْبِلَةِ.
english: The supplies were about to run out, so we expected the herder's return next Friday.
reason: Grammatical and plausible in a context where the herder's return is connected to replenishing supplies; accurately translated.

arabic: نَسِيَ الرَّجُلُ المُنْفَرِدُ كَرُوَاسُونَهُ عَلَى الأَرْضِ، فَتَلَقَّطَتْهُ الطُّيُورُ وَهُوَ يُدَمْدِمُ.
english: The lone man forgot his croissant on the ground, so the birds picked it up as he grumbled.
reason: A coherent, plausible scene; the translation accurately conveys the birds collecting the croissant while the man grumbles.

arabic: الرِّعَايَةُ هَامَّةٌ لِلشِّفَاءِ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَرَضِ، لَكِنَّ الْمُعَانَاةَ بَاقِيَةٌ.
english: Care is important for recovery from this disease, but the suffering persists.
reason: Grammatical and coherent; the translation accurately conveys continuing suffering.

arabic: فِي الْمَطْعَمِ النَّبَاتِيِّ، امْتَزَجَ الْخَرْدَلُ بِالزَّيْتِ الْبَلَدِيِّ فِي وِعَاءٍ صَغِيرٍ.
english: At the vegetarian restaurant, the mustard mixed with the local oil in a small bowl.
reason: A plausible food preparation scene with an accurate translation.

arabic: قَلَعَ الرَّجُلُ شَوْكَةً صَغِيرَةً مِنْ سَبَّابَتِهِ بِآلَةٍ مِنَ الْمَعْدِنِ.
english: The man removed a small thorn from his index finger with a metal instrument.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately describes removing a thorn.

arabic: الْوَلَدُ دَهِشَ مِنْ سِنْجَابٍ صَغِيرٍ تَسَلَّقَ عِمَارَةً مِنَ الطُّوبِ.
english: The boy was astonished by a small squirrel that climbed a brick building.
reason: A natural, coherent description; the English matches the Arabic.

arabic: نَظَّمَ الطُّلَّابُ اسْتِضَافَةَ فِرْقَةٍ أَجْنَبِيَّةٍ فِي قَاعَةِ الْمُؤْتَمَرِ الْحَدِيثَةِ.
english: The students arranged to host a foreign group in the modern conference hall.

arabic: هَلْ شِرَاءُ حَقِيبَةٍ بِهَذَا الْحَجْمِ هَامٌّ لِجَلْبِ كُلِّ الْمَتَاعِ؟
english: Is buying a bag this size important for bringing all the belongings?
reason: A plausible question about bag capacity; the translation preserves its meaning.

arabic: هَاتِ نِصْفَ قِطْعَةِ الزُّبْدَةِ الَّتِي غَلَّفَتْهَا الْجَدَّةُ فِي وَرَقَةٍ.
english: Bring half the piece of butter that Grandma wrapped in paper.
reason: A natural instruction with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِي سِجْنِ مَلِكٍ قَاسٍ، وَقَدْ شَاخَ وَنَحُلَ.
english: The slave was in a cruel king's prison, having grown old and thin.
reason: A plausible narrative sentence; the English accurately conveys his condition.

arabic: عَجِبَ الْوَلَدُ بُرْهَةً مِنْ ضِيَاءِ الْهِلَالِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَأْفُلْ.
english: For a moment, the boy marveled at the glow of the crescent that had not yet set.
reason: Slightly literary but plausible and grammatical; 'had not yet set' fits the Arabic context.

arabic: مَنَحَ الرَّئِيسُ مِلْيُونَ دُولَارٍ لِإِنْشَاءِ صَيْدَلِيَّةٍ لِتَوْفِيرِ الدَّوَاءِ لِلْمُوَاطِنِينَ.
english: The president granted a million dollars to establish a pharmacy to supply medicine to citizens.
reason: A coherent statement about funding a pharmacy, translated accurately.

arabic: رَفَعَ الرَّجُلُ الْفَأْسَ عَلَى الْعُودِ، فَصَاحَ ابْنُهُ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ.
english: The man raised the axe over the piece of wood, and his son cried out in fear.
reason: A plausible scene involving chopping wood; the translation matches the action and reaction.

arabic: لَا تَسْخَرْ مِنْ خَجَلِ الرَّجُلِ، فَأَنْتَ مَغْرُورٌ وَلَسْتَ أَذْكَى مِنْهُ.
english: Do not mock the man's shyness; you are arrogant and no smarter than he is.
reason: A natural rebuke with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: مَقَرُّ الْمِعْمَارِ فِي هَذَا الصَّرْحِ الْإِدَارِيِّ الْبَعِيدِ عَنِ الْمَتْحَفِ.
english: The architect’s headquarters is in this administrative building far from the museum.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; المعمار can mean architect, and the translation matches.

arabic: مِقَصُّ الْحَلَّاقِ مُلَائِمٌ لَهُ، وَمَعَهُ مُشْطٌ فِي هَذَا الدُّرْجِ.
english: The barber’s scissors suit him, and there is a comb with them in this drawer.
reason: A plausible description of a barber’s tools. Singular معه agrees with Arabic مقص; English naturally uses plural scissors.

arabic: أَدْرُسُ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ فِي الْكُلِّيَّةِ، وَقَدْ تَطَوَّرَ نُطْقِي هَذَا الْأُسْبُوعَ.
english: I study phonetics at college, and my pronunciation has improved this week.
reason: Natural learner-friendly Arabic with an accurate translation.

arabic: خَلَطَ النَّادِلُ التُّوتَ بِالْحَلِيبِ، لَكِنَّ الْحَلِيبَ كَانَ مَغْشُوشًا.
